Distinct from funder, which is the entity providing the funding.

candidates.label: fundedItem
candidates.comment: A funded item relation between a grant and the biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product that receives direct or indirect funding or sponsorship. Also called: grant recipient, sponsored item, supported entity. Examples: "Research Grant" funded item "Cancer Research Project", "Arts Grant" funded item "Local Theater Production", "Educational Grant" funded item "Student Scholarship Program". Distinct from funding, which is the grant itself.

candidates.label: recipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation between an action (like sending or paying) and the audience, contact point, organization, or person receiving it. Also called receiver, intended for, sent to. Examples: "A message has a recipient 'John Doe'.", "A donation has a recipient 'Charity Organization'.", "A payment has a recipient 'Vendor Inc.'."

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: endorsee
candidates.comment: An endorsee relation between an endorse action and the person or organization being supported. Also called "supported entity", "beneficiary", "recipient of endorsement". Examples: "Endorse action endorsee 'Candidate A'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Charity B'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Product C'". Distinct from endorsers, which are the people or organizations providing the endorsement.

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.

relations.definition: Indicates the industry or field in which a person is employed.
relations.embedding_query_text: works in: Indicates the industry or field in which a person is employed.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and a person who works for it. Also called "works for", "staff member", "on staff". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employee 'Sundar Pichai'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employee 'Jane Doe'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employee 'Chef John'". Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: industry
candidates.comment: An industry classification relation between a job posting and the sector of economic activity it belongs to. Also called sector, business area, field, domain. Examples: A software engineer job posting has an industry of 'Technology'. A nurse job posting has an industry of 'Healthcare'. A marketing manager job posting has an industry of 'Advertising'.

candidates.label: workLocation
candidates.comment: A work location relation between a person and a contact point or place, identifying where the person performs their professional duties. Also called employment location, office address, workplace. Examples: John workLocation MainOffice, Jane workLocation RemoteHome, CompanyEmployee workLocation BranchOffice. Distinct from homeLocation, which is a person's residential address.

candidates.label: employees
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and the people who work for it. Also called "staff", "workforce", "personnel". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employees 'Thousands of people'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employees 'All its staff'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employees 'Its kitchen and wait staff'". Distinct from members, which indicates general affiliations rather than employment relationships.

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: employmentUnit
candidates.comment: An employment unit relation between a job posting and the organization (department, unit, or facility) where the job is performed. Also called "department", "work unit", "reporting unit". Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' employmentUnit 'Engineering Department'", "Job 'Sales Associate' employmentUnit 'Retail Store #123'", "Job 'HR Specialist' employmentUnit 'Human Resources Division'".

candidates.label: jobTitle
candidates.comment: An occupational role relation between a person and their formal designation within an organization. Also called position, role, occupation, professional title. Examples: A person has a jobTitle of 'Software Engineer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Chief Executive Officer'. A person has a jobTitle of 'Marketing Manager'.

candidates.label: practicesAt
candidates.comment: A professional affiliation relation between an individual physician and the medical organization where they practice. Also called works at, affiliated with, employed by, is a doctor at. Examples: Dr. Smith practices at 'General Hospital'. Dr. Jones practices at 'City Clinic'. The physician practices at 'Family Health Center'.

candidates.label: jobLocation
candidates.comment: An employment location relation between a job posting and the primary geographic place where the work is performed. Also called work location, employment site, job site, place of work. Examples: A job posting has a jobLocation of 'New York City'. A job posting has a jobLocation of 'San Francisco Bay Area'. A job posting has a jobLocation of 'Remote'. Distinct from jobLocationType, which describes the *type* of location (e.g., 'TELECOMMUTE').

relations.definition: Indicates the source of motivation or influence for an idea or action.
relations.embedding_query_text: inspired by: Indicates the source of motivation or influence for an idea or action.

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: isBasedOn
candidates.comment: A derivation relation between a creative work and the resource (another work, product, or URL) from which it is adapted or modified. Also called derived from, adapted from, based on, inspired by, modification of. Examples: A movie isBasedOn 'a novel'. A software update isBasedOn 'previous version'. A remix isBasedOn 'original song'. Distinct from isBasedOnUrl, which specifically points to a URL as the source.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: sender
candidates.comment: The audience, organization, or person initiating and transmitting a message or action. Also called originator, dispatcher, message source, sender of message. Examples: `Email Message` sender `John Doe`, `ReceiveAction` sender `Customer Service`, `Broadcast Message` sender `News Organization`. Distinct from `recipient`, which is the receiving party.

candidates.label: agent
candidates.comment: An agent relation between an action and the organization or person who directly performs or drives it. Also called performer, doer, initiator, actor. Examples: "A 'write book' action's agent is 'John Doe'.", "A 'deliver package' action's agent is 'Delivery Service Inc'."

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

relations.definition: Indicates a past state or role of an entity.
relations.embedding_query_text: was a: Indicates a past state or role of an entity.

candidates.label: roleName
candidates.comment: The specific designation or title of a role performed by a person or organization. Also called role title, position name, function name. Examples: `Person in Movie` roleName `"Actor"`, `Team Member` roleName `"Quarterback"`, `Project Contributor` roleName `"Lead Developer"`.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: character
candidates.comment: A fictional role relation between a creative work and a person who is a character within it. Also called "fictional person", "role played by", "depicted character". Examples: "Novel 'Pride and Prejudice' character Elizabeth Bennet", "Movie 'Star Wars' character Luke Skywalker".

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: actionStatus
candidates.comment: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition. Examples: "A 'purchase' action's action status is 'CompletedActionStatus'.", "A 'shipment' action's action status is 'PotentialActionStatus'."

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

relations.embedding_query_text: was shot in:

candidates.label: workPresented
candidates.comment: A presented work relation between a screening event and a movie, identifying the film shown during that event. Also called screened movie, film shown, featured film. Examples: ScreeningEvent workPresented "The Matrix", FilmFestivalEvent workPresented "Parasite", DriveInMovie workPresented "Jaws". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPerformed, which is for live enactments.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: gameLocation
candidates.comment: A game location relation between a game or video game series and a real or fictional place where the game or part of it is set. Also called: game setting, virtual world, game environment. Examples: "Grand Theft Auto V" game location "Los Santos", "The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild" game location "Hyrule", "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" game location "England".

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: screenshot
candidates.comment: An image or URL depicting a screenshot of a software application. Also called app screenshot, software image, UI capture. Examples: `Mobile App` screenshot `ImageObject of home screen`, `Desktop Software` screenshot `URL to gallery`, `Web Application` screenshot `Image of dashboard`. Distinct from `image`, which is a general image of the item.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: partOfTVSeries
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between a TV episode, season, or clip and the TV series it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is featured in, is from, is a segment of. Examples: A TV episode is part of a TV series. A TV season is part of a TV series. A TV clip is part of a TV series. Distinct from partOfSeries, which is a more general property for any creative work series.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: spokenByCharacter
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a quotation and the character, person, or organization to whom it is attributed within a creative work. Also called "attributed to", "quote speaker", "character says", "uttered by". Examples: "The quote is spokenByCharacter Hamlet", "The dialogue was spokenByCharacter the CEO", "This line is spokenByCharacter a fictional narrator."

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: readBy
candidates.comment: A narration relation between an audiobook and the person who performs the reading. Also called narrated by, performed by, voiced by. Examples: "The audiobook 'Harry Potter' is read by 'Stephen Fry'.", "An autobiography audiobook is read by 'the author'.", "A classic novel audiobook is read by 'a professional narrator'."

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: knownVehicleDamages
candidates.comment: A vehicle condition relation between a vehicle and a textual description of its known damages, whether repaired or not. Also called vehicle damage report, damage history, known defects, condition notes. Examples: A used car has knownVehicleDamages 'minor dent on rear bumper'. A vehicle has knownVehicleDamages 'repaired fender bender'. A truck has knownVehicleDamages 'scratches on passenger side door'. Distinct from vehicleCondition, which is a general assessment, not specific damages.

candidates.label: suggestedGender
candidates.comment: An indication of the recommended gender for an intended person or audience. Also called "target gender", "audience gender", "gender recommendation". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedGender unisex", "The audience specification includes suggestedGender female", "This product is for suggestedGender male."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: suggestedAge
candidates.comment: A quantitative value indicating the recommended age or age range for an intended audience or person. Also called "recommended age", "age range", "target age", "suitable age". Examples: "The toy has suggestedAge 3-5 years", "The audience specification includes suggestedAge 18+", "This product is for suggestedAge 6-12 months.". Distinct from suggestedMinAge and suggestedMaxAge, which specify only the minimum or maximum.
